bull.b: The large financing materially improves execution capacity by funding the lead program through major development milestones. A longer runway reduces near-term financing risk and gives management more time to generate clinical and regulatory value.

bull.t: FDA alignment supports a defined Phase 3 path
bull.b: Agreement with the FDA on one registrational design reduces uncertainty around the pivotal development plan. This clearer path can improve capital allocation, trial execution and the probability of advancing EB613 toward a potential NDA.

bull.t: Oral peptide platform and clinical leadership strengthen execution
bull.b: Evidence supporting comparable pharmacologic effects in a simpler tablet format reinforces the platform’s differentiation. Adding an experienced clinical and regulatory leader should also improve organizational readiness as Entera moves into late-stage development.

bear.t: No meaningful revenue and persistent operating losses
bear.b: Entera has not demonstrated commercial traction or a sustainable revenue base. Continued operating losses leave future value dependent on successful clinical development and eventual commercialization rather than on an established operating franchise.

bear.t: Heavy cash burn requires continued external funding
bear.b: Persistent cash consumption means the company cannot currently finance operations internally. Although recent funding extends runway, future trials, regulatory work and commercialization may still require additional capital if milestones or timelines change.

bear.t: Expanded equity capacity creates material dilution risk
bear.b: The enlarged share authorization and incentive pool provide flexibility for future fundraising and employee compensation, but also increase potential dilution. Existing holders may face a smaller ownership share as development and corporate funding continue.
